1	# Sesh - Smart Tmux Session Manager
2	
3	[Sesh](https://github.com/joshmedeski/sesh) is a CLI that manages tmux sessions using zoxide, giving you instant access to your most-used projects with smart session naming, startup commands, and preview.
4	
5	## Installation
6	
7	Sesh is installed automatically by the `devtools` ansible role:
8	
9	- **macOS**: `brew install sesh`
10	- **Linux**: GitHub release binary → `~/.local/bin/sesh`
11	
12	No manual installation needed after `chezmoi apply`.
13	
14	## Keybindings
15	
16	### ZSH (`Alt+S`)
17	
18	Press `Alt+S` anywhere in the shell to open the sesh picker. This uses `fzf-tmux` as a popup with full filtering support.
19	
20	Source: `~/.config/zsh/tools/22_sesh.zsh`
21	
22	### ZSH Helpers
23	
24	The managed zsh config provides four shell helpers, each with a distinct
25	weight class so you can pick the right tool for the moment:
26	
27	| Command | Weight | When to use | Session name |
28	|---------|--------|-------------|--------------|
29	| `shere` | Bare shell | Ad-hoc cd: just need a tmux session at `$PWD`, no editor, no layout | `<basename>` |
30	| `sroot` | Sesh defaults | Want sesh's wildcard / `default_session` behavior at the git root | sesh-determined (`dir_length=2`) |
31	| `scode` | Heavy | "Open the coding-agent layout for *this* repo" — nvim 75% \| `specstory run` 25% + btop window | `coding-agent/<repo>` |
32	| `svibe` | Heaviest | "Vibe coding" — N tiled agent panes + lazygit + nvim | `vibe/<repo>` |
33	
34	The underlying functions are `sesh-here` / `sesh-root` / `sesh-code` /
35	`sesh-vibe`; you can call them directly if you prefer function names over
36	aliases.
37	
38	#### `shere` — bare shell at `$PWD`
39	
40	Intentionally lightweight: creates a tmux session named after the basename of
41	the directory, drops you into a shell, **does not** trigger sesh's
42	`default_session.startup_command` (nvim) or any wildcard layout. Use it when
43	you've cd'd somewhere ephemeral and just want session persistence.
44	
45	```bash
46	shere                          # bare shell session at $PWD
47	shere npm run dev              # session that runs `npm run dev` instead of a shell
48	shere -c "specstory run"       # explicit --command flag
49	shere -p ~/some/dir            # explicit path; -p + bare args also works
50	```
51	
52	> **Behavior change (2026-04)**: `shere` used to inherit sesh's default
53	> startup_command, which opened nvim. It was renamed to "lightweight session"
54	> because the heavy editor-first workflow is now `scode`. If you want the old
55	> behavior, use `sroot` (which honors the sesh wildcards/defaults) or
56	> `sesh connect "$PWD"` directly.
57	
58	#### `sroot` — git root with sesh defaults
59	
60	Connects to the current git repo's top-level (or `$PWD` if not in a repo) and
61	honors all of sesh.toml: wildcard layouts (e.g. `/Volumes/Data/Program/*/*`
62	auto-applies `project.yaml`), `default_session.startup_command`, etc. This is
63	the right choice if you've been customizing sesh.toml and want those
64	customizations to apply.
65	
66	```bash
67	sroot                          # connect to git root, sesh.toml decides layout
68	sroot specstory run codex      # explicit command override
69	```
70	
71	#### `scode` — repo-scoped coding-agent layout
72	
73	`scode` creates a session **named after the current repo**, so different
74	repos no longer collide on the single `coding-agent` session name. This was
75	the headline pain point of the old `sesh connect coding-agent` workflow:
76	the second invocation from a different repo would silently reuse the
77	existing session pointing at the *wrong* repo.
78	
79	```bash
80	scode                          # current repo, default agent (specstory → claude)
81	scode codex                    # right pane runs `specstory run codex`
82	scode opencode                 # right pane runs `opencode` raw (not yet a specstory provider)
83	scode --no-specstory claude    # right pane runs `claude` raw (no markdown auto-save)
84	scode --on-exit kill claude    # Ctrl+C closes the right pane (vs default: drops to shell)
85	scode --on-exit restart codex  # codex auto-respawns on crash
86	scode -p ~/work/foo            # explicit repo path
87	scode --no-attach              # build the session in the background, don't switch
88	scode -h                       # help
89	```
90	
91	Layout (window 1 "editor"):
92	
93	```
94	┌─────────────────────────────┬──────────────┐
95	│ nvim                        │ specstory    │
96	│ (75% width)                 │ run [agent]  │
97	│                             │ (25% width)  │
98	└─────────────────────────────┴──────────────┘
99	```
100	
101	Window 2 "monitor": `btop` (falls back to `htop` / `top`).
102	
103	**Refuses outside a git repo** — if you're not in a repo, you don't want the
104	heavy layout. Use `shere` for bare shells or `svibe` if you really want a
105	vibe layout in a non-repo directory (svibe also requires a repo, but that's
106	because vibe layouts make even less sense without git context).
107	
108	##### Agent wrapping (auto, opt out with `--no-specstory`)
109	
110	| Argument | Right-pane command |
111	|----------|--------------------|
112	| (none) | `specstory run` (defaults to claude with auto-save md) |
113	| `claude` / `codex` / `cursor` / `droid` / `gemini` | `specstory run <name>` (known specstory providers) |
114	| `opencode` and other unknown CLIs | runs the binary directly |
115	| any agent + `--no-specstory` | runs the binary directly (raw) |
116	
117	> `opencode` is currently raw because specstory upstream doesn't support it
118	> as a provider yet. Tracked in
119	> [`backlog/specstory-opencode-support.md`](../../backlog/specstory-opencode-support.md)
120	> — when `specstoryai/getspecstory#156` lands, the case statement in
121	> `_sesh_wrap_agent` gets a one-line update and opencode joins the auto-wrap
122	> list.
123	
124	##### `--on-exit` modes
125	
126	What happens when **any** pane command exits (agent, nvim, btop in `scode`;
127	agent, lazygit, nvim in `svibe`) — clean quit, Ctrl+C, or crash:
128	
129	| Mode | Behavior |
130	|------|----------|
131	| `shell` (default) | Pane prints a yellow hint and drops into `$SHELL`. You can re-launch the command (the hint shows the exact invocation), switch windows, or close the pane manually. Costs one background `$SHELL` process per pane while the command isn't running. |
132	| `kill` | Pane/window closes when the command exits. The historical / tmux-default behavior. |
133	| `restart` | Wraps the command in `while true; do CMD \|\| true; sleep 1; done`. Use Ctrl+C twice quickly to break the loop and land in shell. Useful when iterating on a crash-prone tool. |
134	
135	> The `shell` default trades one background process per pane for far better
136	> recoverability — the most common reported pain point with the old
137	> `coding-agent` workflow was "I hit Ctrl+C in the agent and lost the pane
138	> plus the 75/25 layout"; the same applies to accidentally `:q`-ing nvim or
139	> quitting btop/lazygit.
140	
141	> The flag applies uniformly to every command-running pane in the layout —
142	> there is no per-surface override. If you want e.g. lazygit to die on quit
143	> but agents to drop to shell, file a feature request.
144	
145	##### Single-agent only
146	
147	`scode` is single-agent by design. If you want multiple agents in parallel,
148	use `svibe --agents …`. Passing `--agents` to `scode` errors with a hint to
149	switch to `svibe`.
150	
151	> The legacy `coding-agent` named session in `sesh.toml` is **kept for
152	> back-compat** (still appears in the sesh picker, still works as
153	> `sesh connect coding-agent`) but `scode` is the preferred entry point.
154	> See the "DEPRECATED" comment block in sesh.toml.
155	
156	#### `svibe` — parametric multi-agent vibe layout
157	
158	Built directly with tmux scripting (not tmuxp) because pane counts are
159	parametric and tmuxp YAML can't express that.
160	
161	Two ways to specify which agents run:
162	
163	```bash
164	# Homogeneous (positional): all panes run the same agent
165	svibe                                            # 4× claude (default)
166	svibe 2                                          # 2× claude
167	svibe 4 codex                                    # 4× codex
168	svibe 6 opencode                                 # 6× opencode (heavy — large monitor recommended)
169	
170	# Heterogeneous (--agents): one entry per pane, list length = pane count
171	svibe --agents claude,codex,codex,opencode       # 4 panes, mixed
172	svibe --agents claude,opencode                   # 2 panes, mixed
173	svibe --agents 'claude, codex, opencode'         # whitespace around commas tolerated
174	
175	# Other flags (work with both modes)
176	svibe --on-exit kill 4 claude                    # Ctrl+C closes panes
177	svibe --on-exit restart --agents codex,opencode  # auto-respawn loop
178	svibe --no-specstory 4 claude                    # 4× raw claude (no markdown auto-save)
179	svibe -p ~/repo --agents claude,codex            # explicit path
180	svibe -h                                         # help
181	```
182	
183	Mixing positional `[N] [CLI]` with `--agents` is **rejected** to keep
184	semantics unambiguous — pick one mode.
185	
186	Layout (3 windows):
187	
188	```
189	window 1 "agents"    — N tiled panes, each running its agent (mixed allowed)
190	window 2 "git"       — lazygit (or `git status` fallback)
191	window 3 "edit"      — nvim
192	```
193	
194	Pane count is bounded `[1, 12]`. Above ~6 the tiled layout becomes too
195	cramped on most displays — the cap is conservative, not technical.
196	
197	##### Validation (fail-fast)
198	
199	`svibe` validates before building anything:
200	
201	1. `--agents` and positional `[N] [CLI]` cannot both be set
202	2. `--on-exit` must be `shell` / `kill` / `restart`
203	3. Pane count in `[1, 12]`
204	4. Must be inside a git repo
205	5. **Every** agent CLI in the list must exist in `$PATH`
206	
207	This avoids the "4-pane window where one pane is silently dead" failure mode
208	you'd get if validation were per-pane.
209	
210	##### `--no-specstory` and `--on-exit`
211	
212	Same semantics as `scode`. The wrapping is **per-pane**, so you can mix
213	opencode (raw) with claude (specstory-wrapped) freely:
214	
215	```bash
216	# 3 panes — opencode raw, claude wrapped, codex wrapped, all share --on-exit shell
217	svibe --agents opencode,claude,codex
218	```
219	
220	Like `scode`, `svibe` refuses outside a git repo. Use `shere` for plain
221	shells in arbitrary directories.
222	
223	### Picking between the four
224	
225	Decision tree:
226	
227	```
228	Are you in a git repo?
229	├── No  → shere (bare shell) or sroot (if you want sesh defaults)
230	└── Yes → Do you want a layout?
231	          ├── No                       → shere or sroot
232	          ├── Single editor + side    → scode
233	          └── Multiple parallel agents → svibe
234	```
235	
236	All four are idempotent: re-invoking with the same target attaches to the
237	existing session instead of creating a duplicate.
238	
239	### tmux
240	
241	All keybindings use the tmux prefix (default `Ctrl+B`).
242	
243	| Keybinding | Action |
244	|------------|--------|
245	| `prefix + g` | Open sesh picker popup (fzf with preview, icons, filtering) |
246	| `prefix + T` | Open sesh picker via television (tv) in a tmux popup |
247	| `prefix + O` | Open sesh built-in picker in a tmux popup |
248	| `prefix + W` | Open sesh window picker (fzf) -- switch or create tmux windows |
249	| `prefix + S` | Switch to last session (via `sesh last`) |
250	| `prefix + 9` | Jump to root of current git repo/worktree |
251	
252	Source: `~/.tmux.conf`
253	
254	`prefix + g` avoids relying on `Shift`, so it does not fall through to tmux's built-in `prefix + t` clock shortcut on terminals that do not report uppercase prefix bindings reliably.
255	
256	### Picker Keybindings (inside fzf popup)
257	
258	| Key | Action |
259	|-----|--------|
260	| `Ctrl+A` | Show all sessions |
261	| `Ctrl+T` | Filter: tmux sessions only |
262	| `Ctrl+G` | Filter: configured sessions only |
263	| `Ctrl+X` | Filter: zoxide directories only |
264	| `Ctrl+F` | Filter: find directories (`fd`) |
265	| `Ctrl+D` | Kill selected tmux session |
266	| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Navigate down/up |
267	
268	## Shell Completion
269	
270	ZSH tab completion for `sesh` subcommands and flags is auto-generated into `~/.zfunc/_sesh` on first load (and regenerated when sesh version changes). This follows the project's [completion pattern](zsh/zsh-completions.md).
271	
272	Manual regeneration:
273	
274	```bash
275	sesh completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_sesh
276	rm -f ~/.zcompdump && compinit
277	```
278	
279	## Configuration
280	
281	Config file: `~/.config/sesh/sesh.toml` (managed by chezmoi)
282	
283	### Schema Autocomplete
284	
285	The config includes a JSON Schema directive for editor autocomplete via [taplo](https://taplo.tamasfe.dev/):
286	
287	```toml
288	#:schema https://github.com/joshmedeski/sesh/raw/main/sesh.schema.json
289	```
290	
291	### Key Options
292	
293	| Option | Description |
294	|--------|-------------|
295	| `sort_order` | Session type display order: `tmux`, `config`, `tmuxinator`, `zoxide` |
296	| `dir_length` | Directory components in session names (default: 1) |
297	| `blacklist` | Regex patterns to hide from the picker |
298	| `cache` | Enable stale-while-revalidate caching (experimental) |
299	
300	### Default Session
301	
302	Applied to all sessions unless overridden:
303	
304	```toml
305	[default_session]
306	startup_command = "nvim"
307	preview_command = "eza --all --git --icons --color=always {}"
308	```
309	
310	- `startup_command`: runs when a new session is created
311	- `preview_command`: shown in the fzf preview pane (`{}` = session path)
312	
313	### Named Sessions
314	
315	Pin frequently used directories with custom names and commands:
316	
317	```toml
318	[[session]]
319	name = "chezmoi"
320	path = "~/.local/share/chezmoi"
321	tmuxinator = "chezmoi"    # delegates to tmuxinator for reliable multi-window setup
322	
323	[[session]]
324	name = "home"
325	path = "~"
326	disable_startup_command = true
327	```
328	
329	Available fields: `name`, `path`, `startup_command`, `preview_command`, `disable_startup_command`, `windows`.
330	
331	### Wildcard Sessions
332	
333	Apply settings to directories matching a glob pattern:
334	
335	```toml
336	[[wildcard]]
337	pattern = "~/repos/*"
338	startup_command = "nvim"
339	```
340	
341	- `*` matches one level, `**` matches recursively
342	- Explicit `[[session]]` entries take priority over wildcards
343	
344	#### Per-project layout via tmuxp `--append`
345	
346	For repos that benefit from a structured layout (editor / shell / lazygit
347	windows), wildcards can chain a `tmuxp load --append` on top of the bare
348	session sesh creates. Same trick as the `coding-agent` named session — see
349	[Approach B below](#approach-b-tmuxp-via-startup_command-active) for the
350	underlying mechanic.
351	
352	```toml
353	# All repos under /Volumes/Data/Program/<group>/<repo>
354	[[wildcard]]
355	pattern = "/Volumes/Data/Program/*/*"
356	startup_command = "cd {} && tmuxp load -a -y ~/.config/tmuxp/project.yaml && tmux kill-window -t :1 2>/dev/null; tmux select-window -t :editor 2>/dev/null"
357	```
358	
359	The `{}` placeholder is the matched path. The leading `cd {}` is
360	load-bearing, and pairs with an equally load-bearing **omission** in the
361	yaml: neither `project.yaml` nor `coding-agent.yaml` sets session-level
362	`start_directory`. Every "obvious" value silently breaks in one of three
363	ways — tmuxp resolves yaml strings via Python's `os.path.expandvars` (no
364	bash `${VAR:-default}` fallback); tmuxp resolves `.` / `./foo` against
365	the yaml **file's** directory (not the process cwd); and when libtmux
366	passes any of those results to `tmux new-window -c`, an invalid path
367	silently falls back to `$HOME`. By omitting `start_directory` entirely,
368	libtmux calls `tmux new-window` without `-c`, so tmux inherits the cwd
369	from the caller — and sesh's `send-keys` runs tmuxp from inside a pane
370	that `cd {}` has already moved to the matched path. Full write-up in
371	[pitfalls/tmuxp-append-ignores-session-start-directory.md](../../pitfalls/tmuxp-append-ignores-session-start-directory.md).
372	
373	After the append, the empty initial window sesh always creates is killed
374	(`-t :1`), and focus moves to the `editor` window so nvim is foregrounded
375	immediately.
376	
377	The pattern targets `/Volumes/Data/Program/*/*` (canonical paths) rather
378	than `~/Documents/Program/*/*` because zoxide records canonical paths
379	(see [zoxide.md](zoxide.md) → `_ZO_RESOLVE_SYMLINKS`). One pattern catches
380	both surface and canonical entries.
381	
382	### Custom multi-section preview
383	
384	The default `eza` preview only shows a file listing. The
385	[`~/bin/sesh-preview`](../../bin/executable_sesh-preview) script renders a
386	richer view in the fzf preview pane:
387	
388	1. **Header**: dir name, parent path, git branch + dirty count + ahead/behind, mtime
389	2. **README**: first 25 lines, syntax-highlighted via `bat` if available
390	3. **Recent commits**: last 5 oneline commits (git repos only)
391	4. **File tree**: `eza --tree --level=2` with build dirs ignored
392	
393	Wired in `sesh.toml`:
394	
395	```toml
396	[default_session]
397	preview_command = "~/bin/sesh-preview {}"
398	```
399	
400	Falls back to plain `head`/`ls` if `bat`/`eza` are missing, and gracefully
401	handles non-directory args (sesh sometimes hands the picker raw session
402	strings rather than paths). Output is capped under ~50 lines to avoid
403	fzf preview pane scroll on first paint.
404	
405	### Windows
406	
407	Define reusable window layouts:
408	
409	```toml
410	[[session]]
411	name = "my-project"
412	path = "~/repos/my-project"
413	windows = ["git"]
414	
415	[[window]]
416	name = "git"
417	startup_script = "lazygit"
418	```
419	
420	## Recommended tmux Settings
421	
422	These are already set in `~/.tmux.conf`:
423	
424	```
425	set -g detach-on-destroy off   # stay in tmux when closing a session
426	bind-key x kill-pane           # skip kill-pane confirmation
427	```
428	
429	## Integration with Other Tools
430	
431	### fzf
432	
433	Sesh's primary picker integration. The `fzf-tmux` wrapper renders fzf inside a tmux popup. Our setup uses `--icons` for Nerd Font glyphs and `sesh preview` for the preview pane.
434	
435	### zoxide
436	
437	Sesh uses zoxide's frecency database to suggest directories. Any directory you `cd` into is automatically tracked and appears in `sesh list -z`.
438	
439	`_ZO_RESOLVE_SYMLINKS=1` (set in
440	[`zsh/tools/20_zoxide.zsh`](../../dot_config/zsh/tools/20_zoxide.zsh)) makes
441	zoxide canonicalise paths before storing them, so symlink-heavy setups
442	(e.g. `~/Documents/Program -> /Volumes/Data/Program`) don't fragment a
443	single physical directory's frecency across two phantom entries. Sesh
444	wildcards should target the canonical pattern (`/Volumes/Data/Program/*/*`)
445	rather than the surface symlink.
446	
447	To bootstrap a fresh DB with the directories you'd like sesh to surface
448	immediately (without waiting for organic `cd` traffic), the simplest path
449	is a one-shot Python script that reads the binary `db.zo` (version 3
450	format: `u32 ver, u64 count, then per-entry: u64 path_len, path bytes,
451	f64 rank, u64 ts`), inserts new entries with `rank=1.0`, and writes back.
452	Existing entries with higher scores are preserved. Sample workflow lives
453	in [pitfalls/zoxide-symlink-fragmentation.md](../../pitfalls/zoxide-symlink-fragmentation.md)
454	if/when that pitfall doc is created.
455	
456	### Neovim (in-editor zoxide picker)
457	
458	For jumping between repos without leaving Neovim, [`nvim/lua/plugins/zoxide-picker.lua`](../../dot_config/nvim/exact_plugins/zoxide-picker.lua)
459	adds a snacks.picker over `zoxide query --list --score`:
460	
461	| Keymap | Action |
462	|--------|--------|
463	| `<leader>fz` | Pick repo, change tab-local cwd via `:tcd` |
464	| `<leader>fZ` | Pick repo, change global cwd via `:cd` |
465	
466	`:tcd` (tab-local) is the default to avoid confusing LazyVim's
467	project-root detection when you have buffers from multiple projects open.
468	Use `:cd` (`<leader>fZ`) when you genuinely want the whole nvim session
469	to follow.
470	
471	### Three project pickers compared
472	
473	LazyVim ends up with **three overlapping but distinct** project-jump
474	entry points. Pick the one that matches your intent:
475	
476	| Where | Trigger | Source | What it does |
477	|-------|---------|--------|--------------|
478	| Inside nvim | `<leader>fp` (or dashboard `p`) | `snacks.picker.projects` — oldfiles git roots + `fd` over `dev` dirs | `:tcd` + `persistence.nvim` restore (last buffers/windows for that cwd) |
479	| Inside nvim | `<leader>fz` / `<leader>fZ` | Full zoxide DB (frecency, 100+ entries) | Pure `:tcd` / `:cd`, no session restore |
480	| Inside tmux | `prefix + g` (sesh fzf) | tmux + sesh.toml + zoxide | Switch/create tmux session, spawn nvim + lazygit fresh |
481	
482	Rough heuristic:
483	
484	- **Already in nvim, want to peek at another repo's file** → `<leader>fz`
485	  (cheap, no session ceremony)
486	- **Already in nvim, want to fully resume work on another repo** →
487	  `<leader>fp` (restores buffers/windows you had last time)
488	- **Outside nvim, want a clean per-repo workspace** → `prefix+g` from tmux
489	  (gets you the layout from `~/.config/tmuxp/project.yaml`)
490	
491	### Configuring the snacks projects picker
492	
493	The defaults look at `~/dev` and `~/projects` (which probably don't exist
494	on your machine), plus oldfiles-derived git roots. To make `<leader>fp`
495	surface every repo under your project home, add it to `dev` —
496	[`projects.lua`](../../dot_config/nvim/exact_plugins/projects.lua) does this
497	for `/Volumes/Data/Program`:
498	
499	```lua
500	{
501	  "folke/snacks.nvim",
502	  opts = {
503	    picker = {
504	      sources = {
505	        projects = {
506	          dev = { "/Volumes/Data/Program" },  -- canonical path, not the symlink
507	          max_depth = 2,                       -- catches <group>/<repo>
508	        },
509	      },
510	    },
511	  },
512	}
513	```
514	
515	To **manually pin** a project that doesn't have a `.git` (or you want it
516	permanently surfaced regardless of `fd` discovery), set `projects` to
517	a list of paths:
518	
519	```lua
520	projects = {
521	  vim.fn.expand("~/.local/share/chezmoi"),
522	  vim.fn.expand("~/.config/nvim"),
523	  "/Volumes/Data/Program/Personal/some-repo",
524	},
525	```
526	
527	Both `dev` (auto-discovered via `fd`) and `projects` (manual list) are
528	merged with oldfiles entries before fzf renders. Snacks dedupes by path.
529	
530	The `confirm = "load_session"` default delegates to `persistence.nvim`
531	(also wired in `projects.lua`); it restores the last buffer/window
532	layout for that cwd. If `persistence.nvim` isn't installed, `load_session`
533	silently falls back to opening the file picker after `:tcd`.
534	
535	### Television (tv)
536	
537	[Television](https://github.com/alexpasmantier/television) has a built-in [sesh channel](https://alexpasmantier.github.io/television/community/channels-unix/#sesh). Television is installed by the `devtools` ansible role (`brew install television` on macOS; Linuxbrew on Linux when available, otherwise skipped with a warning because upstream currently ships only `unknown-linux-gnu` binaries that require glibc ≥ 2.39 — incompatible with Ubuntu 22.04 LTS. See [docs/linux-package-sources.md](../linux-package-sources.md)).
538	
539	**tmux keybinding:** `prefix + T` opens television's sesh channel in a tmux popup.
540	
541	```
542	bind-key "T" display-popup -E -w 80% -h 70% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' Sesh (tv) ' "tv sesh"
543	```
544	
545	Use `Ctrl-s` to cycle through sources (all, tmux, config, zoxide, fd), and `Ctrl-d` to kill the highlighted session.
546	
547	A custom cable channel config at `~/.config/television/cable/sesh.toml` overrides the built-in channel with richer source cycling and actions matching our fzf picker setup.
548	
549	### Raycast (macOS)
550	
551	The [sesh Raycast extension](https://www.raycast.com/joshmedeski/sesh) provides GUI-based session switching outside the terminal.
552	
553	## Customization Tips
554	
555	1. **Add project sessions**: Edit `~/.config/sesh/sesh.toml` (via `chezmoi edit ~/.config/sesh/sesh.toml`) to pin your most-used projects.
556	
557	2. **Wildcard for monorepos**: Use `pattern = "~/work/monorepo/packages/*"` to auto-configure all sub-projects.
558	
559	3. **Per-project startup**: Set `startup_command` to launch dev servers, editors, or TUI tools automatically.
560	
561	4. **Preview with bat**: Use `preview_command = "bat --color=always {}/README.md"` to show project READMEs in the picker.
562	
563	5. **Multiple windows**: Define `[[window]]` entries and reference them in sessions for multi-pane layouts (e.g., editor + lazygit).
564	
565	## Pane Layouts (Advanced)
566	
567	### Sesh Limitations
568	
569	Sesh **cannot** create pane splits natively. Each `[[window]]` gets exactly one pane with one `startup_script`. There is no `panes`, `layout`, `size`, or `ratio` configuration.
570	
571	If you need predefined pane layouts (e.g., "left pane = nvim 75%, right pane = specstory run 25%"), you must use an external tool.
572	
573	### The `tmuxp` Field is Dead Code (as of sesh v2.24)
574	
575	**Important**: The `tmuxp` field in `sesh.toml` (on `[[session]]` and `[default_session]`) is defined in the Go struct and JSON schema, but **never read or used** by sesh's source code. Only `tmuxinator` has a working integration.
576	
577	Evidence from source code:
578	- `startup/config.go` checks `Tmuxinator` and `StartupCommand` but **not** `Tmuxp`
579	- `connector/connect.go` has a `tmuxinatorStrategy` but **no** `tmuxpStrategy`
580	- Setting `tmuxp = "..."` in sesh.toml does nothing -- the session falls through to `default_session.startup_command`
581	
582	### Approach B: tmuxp via `startup_command` (Active)
583	
584	Use sesh's `startup_command` to call `tmuxp load --append`, which appends windows from a tmuxp YAML into the sesh-created session, then kill the initial empty window.
585	
586	Config in `sesh.toml`:
587	```toml
588	[[session]]
589	name = "coding-agent"
590	path = "~"
591	startup_command = "cd ~ && tmuxp load -a -y ~/.config/tmuxp/coding-agent.yaml && tmux kill-window -t coding-agent:1"
592	```
593	
594	(The leading `cd ~` is load-bearing for the same tmuxp-append reason
595	described under the wildcard section above.)
596	
597	Layout defined in `~/.config/tmuxp/coding-agent.yaml`:
598	```yaml
599	session_name: coding-agent
600	windows:
601	  - window_name: editor
602	    layout: main-vertical
603	    options:
604	      main-pane-width: 75%    # 3:1 ratio
605	    panes:
606	      - shell_command: nvim
607	      - shell_command: specstory run
608	  - window_name: monitor
609	    panes:
610	      - shell_command: btop
611	```
612	
613	**How it works:**
614	1. `sesh connect coding-agent` → sesh creates a tmux session named `coding-agent` at `~`
615	2. `startup_command` runs inside the first pane via `tmux send-keys`
616	3. `tmuxp load -a -y` appends the "editor" and "monitor" windows to the current session
617	4. `tmux kill-window -t coding-agent:1` removes the initial empty window sesh created
618	
619	**Pros:** tmuxp already installed, declarative YAML, `--append` avoids session conflict.
620	**Cons:** brief flash of empty window being killed; `startup_command` is `send-keys` so timing-sensitive.
621	
622	**Requires:** `tmuxp` (`pip install tmuxp` or `uv tool install tmuxp`)
623	
624	### Approach C: tmuxinator Native Integration (Alternative)
625	
626	Sesh has full native support for tmuxinator. When `tmuxinator` field is set, sesh **bypasses** its own `NewSession` + `startup.Exec` and delegates entirely to `tmuxinator start`.
627	
628	Config in `sesh.toml`:
629	```toml
630	[[session]]
631	name = "coding-agent"
632	path = "~"
633	tmuxinator = "coding-agent"
634	```
635	
636	Layout defined in `~/.config/tmuxinator/coding-agent.yml`:
637	```yaml
638	name: coding-agent
639	root: <%= @settings["root"] || "~" %>
640	on_project_start: tmux set-window-option main-pane-width 75%
641	windows:
642	  - editor:
643	      layout: main-vertical
644	      panes:
645	        - nvim
646	        - specstory run
647	  - monitor:
648	      panes:
649	        - btop
650	```
651	
652	**How it works:**
653	1. `sesh connect coding-agent` → sesh detects `tmuxinator` field
654	2. `connector/tmuxinator.go` calls `tmuxinator start coding-agent` directly
655	3. tmuxinator creates the entire session with all windows and panes
656	4. sesh then switches/attaches to the session
657	
658	**Pros:** cleanest integration, no empty window hack, sesh natively manages the lifecycle.
659	**Cons:** requires tmuxinator (`gem install tmuxinator`), Ruby dependency.
660	
661	**Requires:** `tmuxinator` (installed by `ruby_gem_tools` ansible role)
662	
663	### Approach A: Pure Shell Script (Fallback)
664	
665	For environments without tmuxp or tmuxinator, use raw tmux commands:
666	
667	```toml
668	[[session]]
669	name = "coding-agent"
670	path = "~"
671	startup_command = "tmux split-window -h -p 25 'specstory run' && tmux select-pane -L && tmux new-window -n monitor 'btop' && tmux select-window -t 1 && nvim"
672	```
673	
674	**Pros:** zero extra dependencies.
675	**Cons:** fragile, hard to read, hard to maintain.
676	
677	### Comparing Approaches
678	
679	Both `coding-agent` (tmuxp) and `coding-agent-mux` (tmuxinator) are configured in `sesh.toml` for A/B comparison:
680	
681	```bash
682	sesh connect coding-agent       # Approach B: tmuxp --append
683	sesh connect coding-agent-mux   # Approach C: tmuxinator native
684	```
685	
686	After testing, keep the one you prefer and remove/comment the other.
687	
688	## try + sesh Integration
689	
690	[try-cli](https://github.com/tobi/try) creates ephemeral project workspaces under `~/src/tries/`. A sesh wildcard automatically applies `startup_command = "nvim"` to any try project.
691	
692	### Usage
693	
694	```bash
695	# One-step: open project and start coding session
696	try-sesh some-project
697	try-sesh https://github.com/user/repo
698	
699	# Two-step: try first, then sesh
700	try some-project
701	shere                    # sesh connect "$PWD"
702	```
703	
704	The `try-sesh` function (alias: `tsesh`) runs `try` then immediately `sesh connect "$PWD"`. Session names follow `dir_length=2` convention: `tries/2026-04-14-some-project`.
705	
706	Source: `~/.config/zsh/tools/32_try.zsh`
707	
708	## Upstream Issues (tmuxp)
709	
710	Sesh's `tmuxp` config field is documented in the schema and README, but **not implemented** in the source code. Relevant upstream issues:
711	
712	- [#87 - Add tmuxp support](https://github.com/joshmedeski/sesh/issues/87) -- Feature request to add tmuxp support. Status: Closed (marked "Done" on project board), but the implementation only added the field to the config struct/schema without wiring it into the connect/startup logic.
713	- [#198 - Built-in Window and Pane management](https://github.com/joshmedeski/sesh/issues/198) -- Request for native pane/window layout support (avoiding tmuxp/tmuxinator dependency). Status: Closed. Sesh v2.25 added basic window support but still no pane splits.
714	- [#188 - startup_command sent too early](https://github.com/joshmedeski/sesh/issues/188) -- Bug where startup_command is sent before the shell is ready. Status: Open. This can affect Approach B (`tmuxp load -a`) if there's a timing issue.
715

```text
68	# implements tmuxinator. See docs/tools/sesh.md for details.

70	# Approach B: tmuxp --append

76	# OMISSION of `start_directory:` in ~/.config/tmuxp/coding-agent.yaml.
77	# tmuxp has three silent-failure modes around `start_directory` that make
78	# every "obvious" yaml value wrong: (a) `os.path.expandvars` doesn't

87	name = "coding-agent"
88	path = "~"

98	# Uses sesh's native tmuxinator integration. Try both and compare:

101	[[session]]
102	name = "coding-agent-mux"
103	path = "~"
104	tmuxinator = "coding-agent-mux"

106	# ── Wildcards ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
107	#
108	# `startup_command` runs after sesh creates the bare session. We use a tmuxp
109	# `--append` invocation that adds the project layout (editor / shell / git
110	# windows) to the session sesh just made, then kills the empty initial window
111	# sesh always creates. Same trick as the `coding-agent` named session above —
112	# see ~/.config/tmuxp/project.yaml for the layout.
113	#
114	# The wildcard `{}` placeholder is the matched path. The leading `cd {}`
115	# is load-bearing and pairs with the deliberate OMISSION of
116	# `start_directory:` in ~/.config/tmuxp/project.yaml. tmuxp has three
117	# silent-failure modes that make every "obvious" yaml value wrong:
118	#   (a) `os.path.expandvars` doesn't understand `${VAR:-default}`,
119	#       leaving it literal.
120	#   (b) `.` / `./foo` are resolved against the yaml FILE's directory
121	#       (tmuxp/cli/load.py:359), not the process cwd — so windows land
122	#       in ~/.config/tmuxp/ instead of the repo.
123	#   (c) When any of those reach `tmux new-window -c` as an invalid path,
124	#       tmux silently falls back to $HOME — no error, no log. (sesh's
125	#       own `tmux new-session -c` still shows up correctly in
126	#       `#{session_path}`, so this looks like a shell-rc / CDPATH bug —
127	#       it isn't.)
128	# By omitting `start_directory` in the yaml entirely, libtmux skips `-c`
129	# and tmux inherits the caller pane's cwd — which `cd {} &&` here
130	# controls. See: pitfalls/tmuxp-append-ignores-session-start-directory.md

136	# so a single wildcard pattern catches both entry points.
```

```text
117	# Build a wrapper command that controls what happens when the inner command
118	# exits (Ctrl+C, agent quit, crash). `--on-exit shell|kill|restart`:
119	#   shell   — print a hint, then drop into $SHELL so user can restart agent,
120	#             switch to lazygit, kill the pane manually, etc. (default)
121	#   kill    — let the pane close on exit (tmux default `remain-on-exit off`)
122	#   restart — wrap in `while true; do CMD; sleep 1; done` so the agent
123	#             auto-respawns. Use Ctrl+C twice quickly to break the loop and
124	#             land in shell.
125	#
126	# Args: $1=inner_cmd, $2=mode, $3=label_for_hint
127	# Stdout: the wrapped shell command (single string suitable for `tmux
128	# new-window … "<cmd>"`). Quoting is structured so user $SHELL is the one
129	# evaluating the inner command — we don't double-eval.
130	function _sesh_on_exit_wrap() {
131	    local inner="$1" mode="$2" label="${3:-agent}"
132	    # Ctrl+C sends SIGINT to the entire foreground process group, so the
133	    # wrapper shell itself dies before it can print the hint or exec the
134	    # login shell — the pane just vanishes. `trap '' INT` makes the wrapper
135	    # ignore SIGINT; the inner command still receives it and exits normally,
136	    # then control returns to the wrapper which prints the hint as intended.
137	    # (Tools that install their own SIGINT handler — btop, htop, less — were
138	    # the visible failure case; agent CLIs happened to handle Ctrl+C as
139	    # clean exit so this was masked for them.)
140	    local guard="trap '' INT;"
141	    case "$mode" in
142	        kill)
143	            print -r -- "$inner"
144	            ;;
145	        restart)
146	            # `|| true` so a crash exit doesn't abort the loop on `set -e` shells
147	            print -r -- "$guard while true; do $inner || true; echo '[$label exited — respawning in 1s; Ctrl+C twice to break]'; sleep 1; done; exec \$SHELL -l"
148	            ;;
149	        shell|*)
150	            # Default. Hint message uses tmux color codes — works in all
151	            # terminals tmux supports.
152	            print -r -- "$guard $inner; printf '\\n\\033[33m[$label exited — back in shell. Re-run with: \\033[1m%s\\033[0;33m]\\033[0m\\n' \"$inner\"; exec \$SHELL -l"
153	            ;;
154	    esac
155	}

397	#                                 positional N_AGENTS is rejected to avoid
398	#                                 ambiguity)

406	#   svibe --agents claude,opencode --on-exit kill  # 2 panes, mixed, hard exit
407	#   svibe --no-specstory 4 claude                  # 4× claude (raw, no md auto-save)
408	#   svibe --on-exit restart 4 codex                # auto-respawn loop
409	#   svibe -p ~/repo 4 claude                       # explicit path
410	#   svibe --no-attach 4 claude                     # create in background

464	  svibe --no-specstory 4 claude                    # raw claude, no auto-save
```

```text
106	# Command-boundary navigation in copy-mode (Warp-style).
107	# Requires OSC 133 markers from the shell — emitted by
108	# dot_config/zsh/tools/02_shell_integration.zsh. In a plain shell (no markers,
109	# e.g. `sh`, `bash` without our hook, or `DISABLE_OSC133=1`), these keys are
110	# no-ops. tmux 3.4+ required for next-prompt/previous-prompt; the `-o` variant
111	# (jump to output start, not prompt start) is tmux 3.5+.
112	#
113	#   {  / }    previous/next prompt (the prompt line itself)
114	#   M-[ / M-] previous/next command output (line AFTER the prompt — usually
115	#             what you want for "skip to the output of the previous command")
116	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
117	bind -T copy-mode-vi '{' send-keys -X previous-prompt
118	bind -T copy-mode-vi '}' send-keys -X next-prompt
119	bind -T copy-mode-vi M-[ send-keys -X previous-prompt -o
120	bind -T copy-mode-vi M-] send-keys -X next-prompt -o

126	# prefix + y: copy visible pane content to system clipboard

129	# over SSH without shelling out to pbcopy/xclip on the remote host.
130	bind y run-shell "tmux capture-pane -p | tmux load-buffer -w - && tmux display-message 'Pane content copied to clipboard'"

144	# empty. Chain: enter copy-mode, jump to start of previous command's output,
145	# begin selection, jump forward to the next prompt (end of output), copy,

148	  send-keys -X previous-prompt -o \; \

337	# zsh functions) and the session-name + switch-client dance is non-trivial.
338	bind -N "scode for current dir (repo-aware coding layout)" 9 \
339	  run-shell -b "~/.config/tmux/scode-here.sh '#{pane_current_path}'"
340	
341	# prefix + 0: lightweight counterpart to prefix+9. Plain sesh session at
342	# the git root of the current pane's directory (no nvim/agent layout).
343	# Replaces tmux's built-in `select-window -t :=0` which always errored
344	# because base-index is 1 (no window 0 exists). Logic in sesh-root-here.sh
345	# — see that file for the two bugs in the original `sesh connect --root
346	# $(pwd)` binding (parse-time $(pwd) + misuse of --root flag).
347	bind -N "sesh-root for current dir (lightweight)" 0 \
348	  run-shell -b "~/.config/tmux/sesh-root-here.sh '#{pane_current_path}'"
349	
350	# prefix + T: sesh picker via television (tv) in a tmux popup
351	bind-key "T" display-popup -E -w 80% -h 70% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' Sesh (tv) ' "tv sesh"
352	
353	# prefix + O: sesh built-in picker in a tmux popup
354	bind-key "O" display-popup -h 90% -w 50% -E "sesh picker -i"
355	
356	# prefix + U: CLI tools picker via television (tv tools)
357	bind-key "U" display-popup -E -w 80% -h 70% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' CLI Tools (tv) ' "tv tools"
358	
359	# (prefix + W is now bound earlier in this file as `kill-window`. The previous
360	# `sesh window` binding was removed because `sesh` has no `window` subcommand;
361	# pressing it printed sesh's help to a popup. See git history.)
362	
363	# =============================================================================
364	# Popup tools (display-popup -E -d '#{pane_current_path}')
365	# =============================================================================
366	# Floating scratch pane (tmux-floax) is on prefix + F (toggleable, persistent
367	# session named `float`). The bindings below are one-shot popups that close
368	# when the inner command exits — handy for "do one thing without disrupting
369	# the layout" workflows.
370	
371	# prefix + G: lazygit popup at current pane path
372	bind-key "G" display-popup -E -w 90% -h 90% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' lazygit ' "lazygit"
373	
374	# prefix + ` (backtick): one-shot popup shell at current pane path.
375	# Closes when the inner shell exits (`exit` or Ctrl-D). Each invocation gets
376	# a fresh shell — no state preserved. For a persistent scratchpad with
377	# history, use floax (prefix + F) instead.
378	bind-key '`' display-popup -E -w 80% -h 80% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' shell '
379	
380	# =============================================================================
381	# Help / cheatsheet
382	# =============================================================================
383	# tmux's built-in `prefix + ?` (list-keys -N) is hard to scan and can't search
384	# user-defined bindings well. We replace it with tmux-fzf's keybinding picker
385	# (fzf popup, fuzzy-searchable). The original list-keys is still reachable on
386	# `prefix + C-?` as a fallback.
387	#
388	# `prefix + /` (built-in: prompt for a key, show what it's bound to) is left
389	# alone — it's already useful for "what does THIS key do?" lookups.
390	#
391	# `?` inside the prefix + Enter popup menu opens a glow-rendered
392	# cheatsheet (curated, grouped, prettier than list-keys).
393	
394	unbind-key '?'
395	bind-key '?' run-shell -b "~/.tmux/plugins/tmux-fzf/main.sh"
396	bind-key 'C-?' list-keys -N
397	
398	# `/` inside the Enter-popup uses this; standalone prefix + / stays built-in
399	# (key-prompt). We expose the cheatsheet through the popup menu's `?` entry.
400	bind-key M-/ display-popup -E -w 80% -h 80% -T ' tmux cheatsheet ' \
401	  "glow -p ~/.config/tmux/cheatsheet.md 2>/dev/null \
402	    || less ~/.config/tmux/cheatsheet.md"
403	
404	# =============================================================================
405	# Popup Menu (prefix + Space)
406	# =============================================================================
407	# Two entry keys, same menu. The menu itself is generated by a script
408	# (`~/.config/tmux/menu.sh`) which:
409	#
410	#   1. Reads `#{client_height}` and emits a tier-trimmed row list. tmux's
411	#      `display-menu` does NOT paginate — if the menu is taller than the
412	#      terminal, the entire popup is silently suppressed (no error). The
413	#      script keeps the menu fitting on tiny mobile-SSH heights too.
414	#   2. Submenus are sibling scripts (menu-layouts.sh, menu-session.sh,
415	#      menu-sesh.sh, menu-popups.sh, menu-theme.sh, menu-system.sh). Each
416	#      `exec tmux display-menu …` so quoting context resets per submenu —
417	#      no nested-quote escaping disasters in keybindings.conf.
418	#
419	# History: an earlier flat ~50-row menu silently failed on smaller heights
420	# and was misdiagnosed as a csi-u key encoding bug, then as a quoting bug.
421	# Both real (the `\;` accelerator was broken, sesh fzf binds had nested-
422	# quote issues), but the dominant symptom — "menu doesn't open at all" —
423	# was actually menu-too-tall. See pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-parse-failure.md.
424	#
425	# Discovery fallbacks if you forget the keys: `prefix + ?` (tmux-fzf fuzzy
426	# picker over every binding), `prefix + M-/` (glow cheatsheet popup), or
427	# right-click on a pane / status line.
428	
429	unbind-key Space
430	unbind-key Enter
431	bind-key Space run-shell "~/.config/tmux/menu.sh"
432	# Note: `prefix + e` was previously a popup-menu alias (added as workaround
433	# for a misdiagnosed display-menu bug — see pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md).
434	# Removed so `e` is free as a sub-menu mnemonic (e.g. "Even layout: horizontal"
435	# in the window right-click menu).
436
```

```text
7	# dropping the entire `display-menu` binding (no error, menu just doesn't

12	# or as a menu row:

14

16	
17	selected="$(
18	  sesh list --icons | fzf-tmux -p 80%,70% \
19	    --no-sort --ansi \
20	    --border-label ' sesh ' \
21	    --prompt '⚡  ' \
22	    --header '  ^a all ^t tmux ^g configs ^x zoxide ^d tmux kill ^f find' \
23	    --bind 'tab:down,btab:up' \
24	    --bind 'ctrl-a:change-prompt(⚡  )+reload(sesh list --icons)' \
25	    --bind 'ctrl-t:change-prompt(🪟  )+reload(sesh list -t --icons)' \
26	    --bind 'ctrl-g:change-prompt(⚙️  )+reload(sesh list -c --icons)' \
27	    --bind 'ctrl-x:change-prompt(📁  )+reload(sesh list -z --icons)' \

30	    --preview-window 'right:55%' \
31	    --preview 'sesh preview {}'
```

```text
1	#!/usr/bin/env zsh
2	# scode-here — open the repo-aware coding-agent layout (`scode`) for the
3	# directory passed as $1 (typically tmux's #{pane_current_path}).
4	#
5	# Bound to `prefix + 9` in dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf. Lives in its
6	# own file because:
7	#   1. tmux run-shell uses /bin/sh and can't see zsh functions/aliases. We
8	#      need an explicit zsh subshell that sources the helper.
9	#   2. The session-name + switch-client logic is non-trivial enough that
10	#      inlining it in keybindings.conf risks the same kind of quoting trap
11	#      as the display-menu case (see pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail).
12	#   3. Easier to debug — `tmux display-message` errors come back via
13	#      $TMUX_LOG below.
14	#
15	# scode itself walks up to find .git via `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`,
16	# so any directory inside a repo works. Outside any repo, scode errors and
17	# we surface that to the tmux status line.
18	#
19	# scode is idempotent: calling it again from inside the same repo just
20	# switches to the existing `coding-agent/<repo>` session.
21	
22	set -eu
23	
24	target_dir="${1:-$PWD}"
25	log="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/tmux-scode-here.log"
26	
27	# Source the helper. ZDOTDIR is respected by chezmoi-managed zsh setup.
28	HELPER="${ZDOTDIR:-$HOME/.config/zsh}/tools/22_sesh.zsh"
29	if [[ ! -r "$HELPER" ]]; then
30	    tmux display-message "scode-here: helper not found at $HELPER"
31	    exit 1
32	fi
33	
34	# shellcheck disable=SC1090
35	source "$HELPER"
36	
37	# Build the session in the background; sesh-code prints diagnostics on
38	# stderr if something fails (not a repo, missing tools, etc).
39	if ! sesh-code --no-attach -p "$target_dir" >"$log" 2>&1; then
40	    err="$(tail -n 1 "$log" 2>/dev/null || echo "(see $log)")"
41	    tmux display-message "scode failed: $err"
42	    exit 1
43	fi
44	
45	# Compute the session name the same way sesh-code does, so we can switch.
46	# _sesh_sanitize and _sesh_git_root are sourced from the helper above.
47	repo_root="$(cd "$target_dir" && _sesh_git_root)"
48	session="coding-agent/$(_sesh_sanitize "$(basename "$repo_root")")"
49	
50	if ! tmux switch-client -t "$session" 2>>"$log"; then
51	    tmux display-message "scode created '$session' but switch-client failed (see $log)"
52	    exit 1
53	fi
54
```

```text
1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# sesh-root-here — open a lightweight sesh session at the git root of $1
3	# (typically tmux's #{pane_current_path}). Unlike scode-here.sh this is a
4	# plain shell at the repo root, no nvim/agent layout — the symmetric
5	# lightweight counterpart to prefix+9 (scode-here.sh).
6	#
7	# Bound to `prefix + 0` and `Ctrl + 0` in keybindings.conf. The previous
8	# `sesh connect --root $(pwd)` inline binding was broken two ways:
9	#   1. $(pwd) was expanded once at tmux config parse time (not per-press),
10	#      so it always pointed at tmux's startup dir.
11	#   2. `--root` is a boolean flag in sesh (switches to root of CURRENT
12	#      session), not "set root dir for new session". The path was being
13	#      treated as a session NAME, which silently created/connected to a
14	#      session named after the path. Probably not what anyone wanted.
15	#
16	# This script does what was actually meant: walk up to find .git, then
17	# `sesh connect <repo-root>`.
18	
19	set -eu
20	
21	target_dir="${1:-$PWD}"
22	
23	# Walk up to find git root; fall back to target_dir if not in a repo.
24	repo_root="$(cd "$target_dir" && git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || true)"
25	if [[ -z "${repo_root:-}" ]]; then
26	    repo_root="$target_dir"
27	fi
28	
29	# `sesh connect <name>` either attaches/switches to existing session or
30	# creates a new one. Idempotent.
31	if ! sesh connect "$repo_root" 2>/tmp/tmux-sesh-root-here.log; then
32	    err="$(tail -n 1 /tmp/tmux-sesh-root-here.log 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)"
33	    tmux display-message "sesh connect failed: $err"
34	    exit 1
35	fi
36
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
117	# Build a wrapper command that controls what happens when the inner command
118	# exits (Ctrl+C, agent quit, crash). `--on-exit shell|kill|restart`:
119	#   shell   — print a hint, then drop into $SHELL so user can restart agent,
120	#             switch to lazygit, kill the pane manually, etc. (default)
121	#   kill    — let the pane close on exit (tmux default `remain-on-exit off`)
122	#   restart — wrap in `while true; do CMD; sleep 1; done` so the agent
123	#             auto-respawns. Use Ctrl+C twice quickly to break the loop and
124	#             land in shell.
125	#
126	# Args: $1=inner_cmd, $2=mode, $3=label_for_hint
127	# Stdout: the wrapped shell command (single string suitable for `tmux
128	# new-window … "<cmd>"`). Quoting is structured so user $SHELL is the one
129	# evaluating the inner command — we don't double-eval.
130	function _sesh_on_exit_wrap() {
131	    local inner="$1" mode="$2" label="${3:-agent}"
132	    # Ctrl+C sends SIGINT to the entire foreground process group, so the
133	    # wrapper shell itself dies before it can print the hint or exec the
134	    # login shell — the pane just vanishes. `trap '' INT` makes the wrapper
135	    # ignore SIGINT; the inner command still receives it and exits normally,
136	    # then control returns to the wrapper which prints the hint as intended.
137	    # (Tools that install their own SIGINT handler — btop, htop, less — were
138	    # the visible failure case; agent CLIs happened to handle Ctrl+C as
139	    # clean exit so this was masked for them.)
140	    local guard="trap '' INT;"
141	    case "$mode" in
142	        kill)
143	            print -r -- "$inner"
144	            ;;
145	        restart)
146	            # `|| true` so a crash exit doesn't abort the loop on `set -e` shells
147	            print -r -- "$guard while true; do $inner || true; echo '[$label exited — respawning in 1s; Ctrl+C twice to break]'; sleep 1; done; exec \$SHELL -l"
148	            ;;
149	        shell|*)
150	            # Default. Hint message uses tmux color codes — works in all
151	            # terminals tmux supports.
152	            print -r -- "$guard $inner; printf '\\n\\033[33m[$label exited — back in shell. Re-run with: \\033[1m%s\\033[0;33m]\\033[0m\\n' \"$inner\"; exec \$SHELL -l"
153	            ;;
154	    esac
155	}

157	# Connect to a sesh session for the current directory (creates it if missing).

165	#   shere -c "specstory run codex"     # explicit --command flag
166	#   shere -p ~/my-proj                 # explicit path, plain shell
167	#   shere -p ~/my-proj npm run dev     # explicit path + command
168	function sesh-here() {
169	    local cmd="" target=""
170	    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
171	        case "$1" in
172	            -c|--command) cmd="$2"; shift 2 ;;
173	            -p|--path)    target="$2"; shift 2 ;;
174	            -*)           echo "sesh-here: unknown flag $1" >&2; return 1 ;;

184	        # shell. We create the session via tmux directly, then attach. This
185	        # also means the wildcard startup_command (project layout) is

187	        # `svibe`, or `sesh connect <path>` for layouts.
188	        local session

192	    fi
193	}

441	  Heterogeneous:  `svibe --agents claude,codex,codex,opencode`

464	  svibe --no-specstory 4 claude                    # raw claude, no auto-save
465	EOF
466	                return 0 ;;
467	            -*)             echo "svibe: unknown flag $1" >&2; return 1 ;;
468	            *)              break ;;
469	        esac
470	    done
471	
472	    # Build the agents array. Two paths:
473	    #   --agents claude,codex,…  → split csv, list length = pane count
474	    #   positional [N] [CLI]     → repeat CLI N times
475	    # Mixing both is rejected to keep semantics unambiguous.
476	    local -a agents
477	    if [[ -n "$agents_csv" ]]; then
478	        if [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; then
479	            echo "svibe: cannot combine --agents with positional N_AGENTS/AGENT_CLI." >&2
480	            echo "       Pick one. (e.g. drop the trailing args)" >&2
481	            return 1
482	        fi
483	        # Split CSV. Trim whitespace per element so 'claude, codex' works.
484	        local IFS=','
485	        agents=( ${=agents_csv} )
486	        # Trim leading/trailing whitespace on each element
487	        local j
488	        for (( j = 1; j <= ${#agents}; j++ )); do
489	            agents[$j]="${agents[$j]## }"
490	            agents[$j]="${agents[$j]%% }"
491	        done
492	        if (( ${#agents} == 0 )); then
493	            echo "svibe: --agents list is empty." >&2
494	            return 1
495	        fi
496	    else
497	        # Positional: [n_agents] [agent_cli]
498	        if [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; then
499	            if [[ "$1" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
500	                n_agents="$1"; shift
501	            fi
502	        fi
503	        [[ $# -gt 0 ]] && agent_cli="$1"
504	        # Build a homogeneous array of length n_agents
505	        local k
506	        for (( k = 1; k <= n_agents; k++ )); do
507	            agents+=( "$agent_cli" )
508	        done
509	    fi
510	
511	    case "$on_exit" in
512	        shell|kill|restart) ;;
513	        *) echo "svibe: --on-exit must be one of: shell, kill, restart (got: $on_exit)" >&2; return 1 ;;
514	    esac
515	
516	    if (( ${#agents} < 1 || ${#agents} > 12 )); then
517	        echo "svibe: agent count = ${#agents} out of range [1, 12]" >&2
518	        return 1
519	    fi
520	
521	    # Resolve repo root
522	    local repo_root
523	    if [[ -n "$target" ]]; then
524	        repo_root=$(cd "$target" 2>/dev/null && _sesh_git_root)
525	    else
526	        repo_root=$(_sesh_git_root)
527	    fi
528	    if [[ -z "$repo_root" ]]; then
529	        echo "svibe: not inside a git repo." >&2
530	        echo "       Use \`shere\` for a plain shell in arbitrary directories." >&2
531	        return 1
532	    fi
533	
534	    # Validate ALL agent CLIs exist in PATH (fail-fast — we don't want to
535	    # build a 4-pane layout where one pane is dead). De-dup the list to keep
536	    # the error message readable.
537	    local -a missing
538	    local -A seen
539	    local a
540	    for a in "${agents[@]}"; do
541	        [[ -n "${seen[$a]:-}" ]] && continue
542	        seen[$a]=1
543	        if ! command -v "$a" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
544	            missing+=( "$a" )
545	        fi
546	    done
547	    if (( ${#missing} > 0 )); then
548	        echo "svibe: agent CLI(s) not found in PATH: ${missing[*]}" >&2
549	        echo "       Available: $(for c in claude codex opencode cursor droid gemini; do command -v $c >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo -n "$c "; done)" >&2
550	        return 1
551	    fi
552	
553	    local repo_name session
554	    repo_name=$(basename "$repo_root")
555	    session=$(_sesh_sanitize "vibe/${repo_name}")
556	
557	    # Idempotent: existing session = just attach
558	    if tmux has-session -t "=$session" 2>/dev/null; then
559	        (( no_attach )) || _sesh_attach_or_switch "$session"
560	        return 0
561	    fi
562	
563	    # Build wrapped command for each agent (the wrapping is pane-specific so
564	    # we can mix providers in one window).
565	    #
566	    # Helper: turn agent name → fully-wrapped tmux command string.
567	    _vibe_agent_cmd() {
568	        local inner
569	        inner=$(_sesh_wrap_agent "$1" "$specstory_mode")
570	        _sesh_on_exit_wrap "$inner" "$on_exit" "$1"
571	    }
572	
573	    # ── Build the session ───────────────────────────────────────────────
574	    # Window 1: agents (start with first pane running agents[1])
575	    tmux new-session -d -s "$session" -c "$repo_root" -n agents \
576	        "$(_vibe_agent_cmd "${agents[1]}")"
577	
578	    # Add remaining panes
579	    local i
580	    for (( i = 2; i <= ${#agents}; i++ )); do
581	        tmux split-window -t "${session}:agents" -c "$repo_root" \
582	            "$(_vibe_agent_cmd "${agents[$i]}")"
583	        # Re-tile after each split so layout stays balanced
584	        tmux select-layout -t "${session}:agents" tiled >/dev/null
585	    done
586	
587	    unset -f _vibe_agent_cmd
588	
589	    # Window 2: git (lazygit if present)
590	    # lazygit and nvim get the same on-exit handling as agents — quitting
591	    # them drops to shell with a re-launch hint rather than killing the window.
592	    local git_cmd edit_cmd
593	    if command -v lazygit >/dev/null 2>&1; then
594	        git_cmd=$(_sesh_on_exit_wrap "lazygit" "$on_exit" "lazygit")
595	        tmux new-window -t "$session" -n git -c "$repo_root" "$git_cmd"
596	    else
597	        # `git status; exec $SHELL` already lands in shell — no wrap needed.
598	        tmux new-window -t "$session" -n git -c "$repo_root" "git status; exec \$SHELL"
599	    fi
600	
601	    # Window 3: edit (nvim)
602	    edit_cmd=$(_sesh_on_exit_wrap "nvim" "$on_exit" "nvim")
603	    tmux new-window -t "$session" -n edit -c "$repo_root" "$edit_cmd"
604	
605	    # Focus agents window, first pane
606	    tmux select-window -t "${session}:agents"
607	    tmux select-pane -t "${session}:agents.1"
608	
609	    (( no_attach )) || _sesh_attach_or_switch "$session"
610	}
```

```text
## FINDINGS REPORT: Tmux Popup Menu & Session Switching System

### 1. Existing Project/Session Picker Menu Entries

The tmux popup menu system (`prefix + Space`) is tiered to fit small screens. Here are all session/project switching entries:

**Tier 0 (always shown):**

**Tier 1 (height ≥22):**

- **`prefix + 9`** (line 338) → `scode-here.sh` — coding-agent layout (nvim 75% + specstory 25%)
- **`prefix + T`** (line 351) → `tv sesh` (television picker)
- **`prefix + O`** (line 354) → `sesh picker -i` (built-in sesh UI)

- **`prefix + S`** (line 329) → `sesh last` (switch to previous sesh session)
- **`prefix + G`** (line 372) → lazygit popup (not session switching, but related git workflow)

### 2. Zoxide Integration & Directory Picker Status

**Current state:** Zoxide IS integrated, but ONLY within sesh picker's filter modes, not as a standalone tmux binding.

- **`sesh-picker.sh`** (line 28) includes `--bind 'ctrl-x:change-prompt(📁  )+reload(sesh list -z --icons)'` — zoxide directories appear as one filter mode
- **No standalone `prefix + Z` or directory-only picker** — the workflow expects users to:
  1. Use sesh picker + Ctrl+X to filter zoxide dirs, then attach/create session there
  2. OR use `cd` + `sroot` / `shere` to land in arbitrary dir then create session

**Gap identified:** No "pick arbitrary directory (zoxide or fd) and create barebone session" one-key binding. The current design assumes you either:
- Know the project name (type in sesh picker)
- Have a git root (use `sroot` from inside it)
- Or explicitly `cd` first, then `sroot`

### 3. In-tmux vs Outside-tmux Session Switching

**Both `shere` and `sroot` detect `$TMUX`:**

From `docs/tools/sesh.md` (lines 58–69):
> `sroot` — Connects to the current git repo's top-level (or `$PWD` if not in a repo) and honors all of sesh.toml: wildcard layouts, `default_session.startup_command`, etc.

The underlying `sesh connect` command (used by `sesh-root-here.sh` line 31) **is idempotent and environment-aware**:
- If `$TMUX` is set (inside a session), `sesh connect <path>` switches the current client to that session
- If `$TMUX` is unset (outside tmux), it attaches to that session or creates + attaches

**Evidence:** `sesh-root-here.sh` (line 31) runs `sesh connect "$repo_root"` with no special branching on `$TMUX` — sesh handles both cases automatically.

The script then calls `tmux switch-client -t "$session"` only after successful session creation (not shown as a fallback). The switch is optional because sesh already did it.

### 4. Unified Project Dashboard

**No unified dashboard exists.** The system is **hierarchical and siloed**:

- **`prefix + Space` → menu.sh** — hierarchical submenu structure (Tier 0/1/2 based on height)
- **Each submenu** is a separate `display-menu` popup (Session, Sesh+, Layouts, Popups, Theme, System)
- **No grid/matrix of "all open sessions + available projects + worktrees"** — would exceed tmux's silent-fail popup height limit

**Cross-references in menus:**
- Session submenu (`menu-session.sh`) offers "New session", "Rename", "Kill", but NO "pick from zoxide/recent" entry
- Sesh+ submenu (`menu-sesh.sh`) offers sesh filters + scode + tv tools
- No single "mega-dashboard" that consolidates both tmux sessions and zoxide frecency in one view

### 5. Documentation on Project Switching Workflow

**Yes, comprehensive docs exist:**

**`docs/tools/sesh.md`** (732 lines):
- Sections: ZSH keybindings (Alt+S), ZSH helpers (shere/sroot/scode/svibe), tmux bindings (prefix+g/T/O/S/9/0), picker keybindings, configuration, integration with zoxide/neovim/television
- **Key quote (lines 240–250):**
  > | Keybinding | Action |
  > |:---|:---|
  > | `prefix + g` | Open sesh picker popup (fzf with preview, icons, filtering) |
  > | `prefix + T` | Open sesh picker via television (tv) in a tmux popup |
  > | `prefix + O` | Open sesh built-in picker in a tmux popup |
  > | `prefix + S` | Switch to last session (via `sesh last`) |
  > | `prefix + 9` | Jump to root of current git repo/worktree |

**`docs/tools/worktrunk.md`** (450+ lines):
- Documents the **three-layer navigation model**: sesh (project) → wt (worktree) → wtcd (peek without session switch)
- Section "Per-worktree Claude / OpenCode" (lines 143–150+) describes aliases like `wt cc` (Claude + worktree) and `wt oc` (OpenCode + worktree)
- **Key integration note (end of file):** References back to sesh.md for the repo layer

**Key workflow quote from worktrunk.md (lines 94–99):**
> | I want to... | Use | What it does | Side effects |
> |:---|:---|:---|:---|
> | Switch **project** | `Alt+S` (sesh picker), `sroot`, `scode` | Detaches from current tmux session, attaches to project's session | Full session swap |
> | Switch **worktree** in current project | `wt switch <branch>` | `cd`s parent shell, runs hooks | New dir |
> | **Peek** at sibling worktree | `wtcd` | `cd`s parent shell only | Stays in same tmux/sesh session |

**No standalone "development workflow" doc** (e.g., `docs/workflow.md` or `docs/my-flow.md`), but the sesh.md and worktrunk.md files together describe the full end-to-end flow.

| No "pick zoxide dir + create session" one-key | Use `sesh picker → Ctrl+X` or `cd $dir && sroot` | Add `prefix + Z` → fzf zoxide + `sesh connect` |
```

```text
4	# On macOS, fzf is managed by Homebrew (/opt/homebrew/bin/fzf) — prepending
5	# ~/.fzf/bin would shadow brew with a stale clone. The chezmoi external that
6	# clones https://github.com/junegunn/fzf is gated to non-darwin in
7	# .chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl for the same reason.
8	if [[ "$OSTYPE" == linux* && -d "$HOME/.fzf/bin" ]]; then

70	            else

72	            fi
```

```text
5	# which conflict with fzf's shell integration.

10	#   Alt+G  tv git-log           (git log browser)
11	#   Alt+E  tv env               (environment variables)
12	#   Alt+A  tv aliases           (all aliases & functions)
13	#   Alt+I  tv git-ops           (insert git command from VSCode/GitLens menu)

15	# fzf keeps Ctrl+T / Ctrl+R / Alt+C (muscle memory).
16	# tv gets Alt namespace for advanced pickers.

19	# so that `tv aliases` channel can read it without spawning `zsh -ic`
20	# (which causes tty suspend issues).
21	#
22	# See: https://github.com/alexpasmantier/television

24	command -v tv &>/dev/null || return 0

26	# --- Tab completion (written to ~/.zfunc/, picked up by compinit) ---

29	  if [[ ! -f ~/.zfunc/_tv ]] || ! grep -q "${_tv_ver}" ~/.zfunc/_tv 2>/dev/null; then
30	    tv completions zsh > ~/.zfunc/_tv 2>/dev/null
31	  fi
32	fi

34	# --- Generate aliases cache for tv aliases channel ---
35	{
36	  mkdir -p ~/.cache/tv
37	  {
38	    alias | while IFS="=" read -r name rest; do
39	      printf "%-22s  alias   %s\n" "$name" "$rest"
40	    done
41	    typeset -f + | while read -r name; do
42	      printf "%-22s  func\n" "$name"
43	    done
44	  } | sort > ~/.cache/tv/aliases.txt
45	} &>/dev/null &!
46	
47	# --- Custom ZLE widgets for tv channels ---
48	
49	_tv_channel_widget() {
50	  emulate -L zsh
51	  zle -I
52	  local output
53	  output=$(tv "$1" --no-status-bar --inline < /dev/tty)
54	  zle reset-prompt
55	  if [[ -n $output ]]; then
56	    LBUFFER+="$output"
57	  fi

66	  zle reset-prompt
67	  if [[ -n $output ]]; then
68	    RBUFFER=""
```

```text
1	# 11_tools_picker.zsh - Interactive CLI tools picker (fzf ZLE widget)
2	# Reads ~/.config/docs/tools/cli-tools.md for the tool list (deployed by chezmoi).
3	#
4	# Alt+T  →  open picker
5	#   Enter      paste invocation to shell buffer (you still press Enter to run)
6	#   Ctrl+E     execute the tool directly (good for TUI apps: btop, lazygit, etc.)
7	#   Ctrl+/     toggle preview panel (shows tldr or --help)
8	#
9	# The invocation for tools that need arguments has a trailing space,
10	# so pressing Enter pastes e.g. "rg " — cursor lands after the space,
11	# ready for you to type your arguments.
12	
13	_TOOLS_DOC="${HOME}/.config/docs/tools/cli-tools.md"
14	
15	# Bail silently if the data file hasn't been deployed yet or fzf is missing
16	[[ -f "$_TOOLS_DOC" ]] || return 0
17	command -v fzf &>/dev/null || return 0
18	
19	# Parse the markdown tables into "INVOCATION<TAB>DESCRIPTION" lines.
20	# Tab separator preserves the trailing space in invocations like "rg ".
21	_tools_list() {
22	    awk -F'|' '/^[[:space:]]*\|[[:space:]]*`/ {
23	      inv=$3; sub(/^[[:space:]]*`/,"",inv); sub(/`[[:space:]]*$/,"",inv)
24	      desc=$4; sub(/^[[:space:]]*/,"",desc); sub(/[[:space:]]*$/,"",desc)
25	      printf "%s\t%s\n", inv, desc
26	    }' "$_TOOLS_DOC"
27	}
28	
29	# ZLE widget: opens fzf picker, pastes selected invocation to the shell command line.
30	tools-picker() {
31	    {
32	        exec </dev/tty
33	        exec <&1
34	
35	        local selected
36	        selected=$(
37	            _tools_list | fzf \
38	                --ansi \
39	                --border \
40	                --prompt ' tools  ' \
41	                --header 'Enter: paste  Ctrl+E: execute  Ctrl+/: preview' \
42	                --delimiter=$'\t' \
43	                --with-nth=1,2 \
44	                --preview 'tool=$(printf "%s" {1} | awk "{print \$1}" | sed "s/ *$//"); (command -v tldr >/dev/null 2>&1 && tldr "$tool" 2>/dev/null) || "$tool" --help 2>&1 | head -50' \
45	                --preview-window='right:55%:wrap:hidden' \
46	                --bind='ctrl-/:toggle-preview' \
47	                --bind='ctrl-e:execute(eval $(printf "%s" {1} | awk "{print \$1}"))+abort'
48	        )
49	
50	        zle reset-prompt >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
51	        [[ -z "$selected" ]] && return
52	
53	        # Extract the invocation (field 1 before the tab), preserving trailing space
54	        local invocation
55	        invocation=$(printf '%s' "$selected" | cut -f1)
56	
57	        # Paste to shell command line buffer without executing
58	        LBUFFER="${LBUFFER}${invocation}"
59	        zle redisplay
60	    }
61	}
62	
63	zle -N tools-picker
64	
65	# Alt+T (mnemonic: Tools)
66	# Alt+S = sesh-sessions, Alt+C = fzf cd — Alt+T is free
67	bindkey -M emacs '\et' tools-picker
68	bindkey -M viins '\et' tools-picker
69	bindkey -M vicmd '\et' tools-picker
```

```text
1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Top-level tmux popup menu — invoked by `prefix + Space`.
3	#
4	# Why a script (not inline `display-menu` in keybindings.conf):
5	#   1. tmux's command parser stops at literal `;`, `{`, `}` even inside
6	#      nested quotes. With ~50 menu rows full of fzf binds and shell
7	#      one-liners, escaping became fragile and broke silently.
8	#   2. tmux `display-menu` does not paginate. If the menu is taller than
9	#      the terminal, the entire popup is suppressed with no error. By
10	#      generating the menu here we can read $TMUX client_height and
11	#      auto-trim low-frequency rows when small.
12	#   3. Submenus are normal `tmux display-menu` invocations from rows;
13	#      they don't share quoting context with the parent menu.
14	#
15	# Submenus live in sibling scripts:
16	#   menu-layouts.sh, menu-session.sh, menu-sesh.sh,
17	#   menu-popups.sh, menu-theme.sh, menu-system.sh
18	#
19	# See: pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-parse-failure.md
20	
21	set -euo pipefail
22	
23	H=$(tmux display-message -p '#{client_height}')
24	DIR=~/.config/tmux
25	
26	# Tier 0: ALWAYS shown (highest frequency, ~7 rows + 2 separators)
27	declare -a tier0=(
28	  "Last window"  Tab "last-window"
29	  "Last pane"    P   "last-pane"
30	  ""             ""  ""
31	  "Choose win"   w   "choose-tree -Zw"
32	  "Choose sess"  s   "choose-tree -Zs"
33	  "Pane #s"      q   "display-panes -d 0"
34	  ""             ""  ""
35	  "Sesh picker"  g   "run-shell '$DIR/sesh-picker.sh'"
36	  "Lazygit"      G   "display-popup -E -w 90% -h 90% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' lazygit ' 'lazygit'"
37	)
38	
39	# Tier 1: shown when height >= 22 (adds new-window/split/zoom)
40	declare -a tier1=(
41	  ""             ""  ""
42	  "New window"   c   "new-window -c '#{pane_current_path}'"
43	  "Split |"      "|" "split-window -h -c '#{pane_current_path}'"
44	  "Split -"      "-" "split-window -v -c '#{pane_current_path}'"
45	  "Zoom"         z   "resize-pane -Z"
46	)
47	
48	# Tier 2: submenus + cheatsheet (always shown if Tier 1 is shown)
49	declare -a tier2=(
50	  ""             ""  ""
51	  "→ Layouts"    L   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-layouts.sh'"
52	  "→ Session"    S   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-session.sh'"
53	  "→ Sesh+"      E   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-sesh.sh'"
54	  "→ Popups"     o   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-popups.sh'"
55	  "→ Theme"      T   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-theme.sh'"
56	  "→ System"     Y   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-system.sh'"
57	  ""             ""  ""
58	  "Cheatsheet"   "?" "display-popup -E -w 80% -h 80% -T ' tmux cheatsheet ' 'glow -p $DIR/cheatsheet.md 2>/dev/null || less $DIR/cheatsheet.md'"
59	  "Search keys"  "/" "run-shell -b ~/.tmux/plugins/tmux-fzf/scripts/keybinding.sh"
60	)
61	
62	rows=("${tier0[@]}")
63	if [ "$H" -ge 22 ]; then
64	  rows+=("${tier1[@]}" "${tier2[@]}")
65	elif [ "$H" -ge 14 ]; then
66	  rows+=("${tier2[@]}")
67	fi
68	
69	exec tmux display-menu -T "#[align=centre,bold]tmux (h=$H)" -x R -y P "${rows[@]}"
70
```
